name: mosquitto
description: Lightweight MQTT broker with authenticated access and persistent configuration

fields.name: MQTT_USER
fields.label: R1: MQTT Username
fields.help: Username created for authenticated MQTT connections when the password file is first generated.

fields.name: MQTT_PASSWORD
fields.label: R2: MQTT Password
fields.help:
Password created when Mosquitto starts for the first time. Save it securely.
Important: Changing this field later does not replace credentials in an existing password.txt file.

fields.name: CONFIG_LOCATION
fields.label: R3: Config Folder
fields.help: Host folder for mosquitto.conf and the generated password file. Existing files are preserved on restart.

fields.name: DATA_LOCATION
fields.label: R4: Data Folder
fields.help: Host folder for Mosquitto's persistent message database.

fields.name: LOG_LOCATION
fields.label: R5: Log Folder
fields.help: Host folder for the persistent Mosquitto log file. Broker messages are also sent to the container log.

fields.name: MQTT_PORT
fields.label: R6: MQTT Port
fields.help: Host port MQTT clients use in bridge mode. In Host Mode, Mosquitto listens directly on NAS port 1883.

fields.name: MOSQUITTO_NETWORK_MODE
fields.label: O1: Network
fields.help: Bridge mode is recommended because MQTT clients can connect using the NAS IP and published port. Host Mode is available but normally does not improve device discovery because Mosquitto itself does not discover devices.

fields.name: RESTART_POLICY
fields.label: O2: Restart Policy
fields.help: Controls whether the broker restarts automatically.

fields.name: MOSQUITTO_IMAGE
fields.label: A1: Image
fields.help: Official Eclipse Mosquitto image. Change this only if you need a pinned version or another image source.

fields.name: MOSQUITTO_PORT_MAPPING
fields.label: A2: Bridge Port Mapping
fields.help: Automatically generated in bridge or existing-network mode and removed in Host Mode.

fields.name: MOSQUITTO_CONTAINER_NAME
fields.label: Container Name
fields.help: EasyDocker sets the container name from the project name.

fields.name: MOSQUITTO_INTERNAL_PORT
fields.label: Internal MQTT Port
fields.help: Recipe-managed MQTT listener port inside the container.

fields.name: MOSQUITTO_SHELL
fields.label: Startup Shell
fields.help: Recipe-managed shell used for first-run initialization.

fields.name: MOSQUITTO_START_SCRIPT
fields.label: First-Run Startup Script
fields.default: set -e; mkdir -p /mosquitto/config /mosquitto/data /mosquitto/log; if [ ! -f /mosquitto/config/mosquitto.conf ]; then printf '%s\n' 'listener 1883' 'allow_anonymous false' 'password_file /mosquitto/config/password.txt' 'persistence true' 'persistence_location /mosquitto/data/' 'log_dest stdout' 'log_dest file /mosquitto/log/mosquitto.log' > /mosquitto/config/mosquitto.conf; fi; if [ ! -s /mosquitto/config/password.txt ] || ! grep -q '^[^:][^:]*:' /mosquitto/config/password.txt; then mosquitto_passwd -b -c /mosquitto/config/password.txt "$$MQTT_USER" "$$MQTT_PASSWORD"; fi; chown -R 1883:1883 /mosquitto/config /mosquitto/data /mosquitto/log; chmod 600 /mosquitto/config/password.txt; chmod 644 /mosquitto/config/mosquitto.conf; chmod 755 /mosquitto/config /mosquitto/data /mosquitto/log; exec /docker-entrypoint.sh mosquitto -c /mosquitto/config/mosquitto.conf
fields.help: Creates the configuration and password file when missing, automatically replaces an invalid empty-username password file, assigns the bind-mounted folders and files to Mosquitto UID/GID 1883, applies secure file modes, and then starts Mosquitto through the image's official entrypoint.

ui.overview: Eclipse Mosquitto is a lightweight MQTT message broker commonly used by Home Assistant, IoT devices, sensors, and automation services.
what_happens: One Eclipse Mosquitto container will be created
Anonymous MQTT access will be disabled
The selected MQTT username and generated password will be written to a password file on first startup
A secure basic mosquitto.conf will be generated only when one does not already exist
Configuration, broker data, and logs will be stored in bind-mounted host folders
Existing configuration and password files will be preserved during restarts and image upgrades
Config, data, and log ownership will be corrected for the Mosquitto service account on every startup
An invalid password file containing an empty username from an earlier recipe version will be regenerated automatically
Bridge networking is selected by default, with Host Mode and existing Docker networks also available
Changing the username or password fields after first deployment does not update the existing password file
ui.data_location: The config, data, and log folders can be relative to this app's config folder or absolute host paths. Back up the config folder because it contains the MQTT password file.
